A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEPA study and contain 43 pages, including complete appendices A–K. Text and visual inspection support a reliable comparison; pages 5–43 render identically.

before.justification: v1 reports original BEPA experiments on OSWorld-Verified, MMBench-GUI, and Online-Mind2Web, together with ablations, sensitivity analyses, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and case studies reported in v1.

M1.justification: The two-stage method is unchanged: plan-conditioned self-rolling initializes guidance, and a dynamically refreshed cache supplies trajectories upon total on-policy failure. Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OSWorld-Verified training and evaluation coverage, MMBench-GUI L1/L2 evaluation, and Online-Mind2Web tasks. No domains or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and the appendix benchmark tables, including SFT, GRPO, RL+SFT, SFT+RL, Trace Replacement, and LUFFY.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same splits, metrics, and evaluation procedures, including the default rollout group size of 8 and OSWorld's 15-step episode limit.

E4.justification: The LEVEL-1/LEVEL-2 ablations, distribution and training-dynamics analyses, expert/backbone comparisons, rollout/cache sensitivity tests, domain breakdowns, and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run mean and standard-deviation reporting in Tables 1 and 12, seed information, and distinction from best-single-run results in Table 7.

E6.justification: All reported results are unchanged. Table 1 retains BEPA's 32.13% overall success and 10.30% held-out success; appendix numerical results and qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Sections 3–4 are unchanged, as are Appendix B's assumptions, variance bound, convergence theorem, and proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about expert–policy mismatch, bi-level assimilation, and improvements across the three benchmarks.

C2.justification: The explanations of static-guidance failures and dynamic alignment are retained. Section 7's applicability limitations and the appendix discussions of difficult domains and case studies are unchanged.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, baseline implementation details, action interfaces, prompt templates, and codebase documentation in Appendices E–F are unchanged. Both versions provide the same code and data access link.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged. Citations shifting between columns or pages in the opening sections are reflow rather than additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 adds Zezhou Wang's Microsoft Research Asia internship note and removes Zhuzhong Qian's corresponding-author designation. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised author footnote changes front-page spacing and causes limited text reflow across pages 1–4. Figures, tables, captions, and all subsequent page layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 changes author notes and the version stamp, with minor layout consequences. The methods, evidence, theory, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
